title: Heterochromatic 3D genome organization is directed by HP1a- and H3K9-dependent and independent mechanisms
Transcription-independent TFIIIC-bound sites cluster near heterochromatin boundaries within lamina-associated domains in C. elegans
Advancements in mapping 3D genome architecture
plainLanguageSummary: DNA is non-randomly distributed in the 3-dimensional space of the nucleus. Scientists have historically studied this non-random genome architecture by microscopy-based techniques. With the development of genomics came assays to map genome architecture with DNA-sequence level resolution. This paper reviews those assays and compares the molecular details underlying them. Assays covered: Chromosome Conformation Capture assays (including Hi-C), SPRITE, and Trac-looping.
